releaseGate.reason: Current source/local integration relies on third-party integration material whose public redistribution and standalone replacement are not fully resolved; native gameplay acceptance is also incomplete.

components.notes: Only runtime files needed by the selected build belong in the player artifact; tests, reports, staging state and source-only tooling stay out.
Recorded license permits redistribution with notices; bundled third-party notices still require release audit.
Prefer pinned, hash-verified official archive contents if bundling is approved.
Do not include unrelated framework extras merely because they ship in the upstream archive unless they are required by the framework.
Bundle only if required by the final realpass runtime.
If the final settings/UI no longer requires it, remove rather than carrying it as baggage.
Currently expected to support one realpass settings surface; reassess if a smaller native settings implementation replaces it.
Retain only if final realpass controls require it. Never package the user's live inputUserMappings.xml.

Current body integration uses Dark Future as a host. Final single-mod work should retain only in-scope adapted material with required attribution/share-alike compliance or replace it with realpass-owned equivalents.

Current recorded permission model requires the original mod and prohibits standalone redistribution of modified assets. Final one-download realpass therefore needs a realpass-owned/recreated presentation path or separately obtained permission.
No Cyberpunk executable, stock archives, compiled cache, saves or user settings enter the release artifact.

artifactRequirements: Game-root-relative paths only for runtime payload.
A short INSTALL.txt at the archive root explains where to extract and how to launch normally.
A VERSION/BUILD identifier and SHA-256 checksum are generated by CI.
Required license and attribution notices are included without development-only files.
The artifact content list is generated and verified before upload.
Blocked dependencies cause the public-playable release job to fail closed rather than silently producing a partial mod.
